heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P can print Prusament PC Blend at speeds up to 143 mm/s capped by a 12 mm³/s volumetric flow limit, but printing large parts reliably requires a dedicated enclosure due to the open-frame design. Additionally, the bed must be run at its absolute maximum of 100°C to mitigate warping, alongside a PVP glue stick barrier on the build plate.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP Glue Stick (mandatory release agent)
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 12 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap travel and extrusion speeds safely at or below 143 mm/s.
Set Bed Temperature to 100°C for all layers (hardware ceiling) and turn off the auxiliary chassis fan entirely to prevent severe thermal draft warping.
Configure a 6-8 mm outer brim with a 0.0 mm brim-object gap to mechanically anchor outer perimeters to the build sheet.
Limit Part Cooling Fan to 0% minimum and 15% maximum, keeping cooling completely disabled for the first 4 layers to maximize interlayer bonding.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe Corner Lifting and Plate Detachment
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Thermal contraction caused by draft exposure from the open P1P frame combined with bed temps limited to 100°C.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install an enclosure or draft shield around the P1P, apply a fresh layer of PVP glue stick, and set a mouse-ear or 8mm brim with 0mm gap in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speed or open-air drafts preventing polymer chains from fusing at the layer boundary.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off the auxiliary chamber fan completely, reduce part cooling fan to 0-10%, and raise nozzle temperature to 280°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Exceeding the 12 mm³/s volumetric capacity of the stock stainless hotend or unbaked moisture in the filament.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool at 75-80°C for 8 hours and verify that maximum volumetric speed in OrcaSlicer does not exceed 12 mm³/s.

faq.question: Can I print Prusament PC Blend on an un-enclosed Bambu Lab P1P?
faq.answer: Small models under 50mm can be printed successfully, but larger technical components will rapidly warp and delaminate without an enclosure to trap ambient heat.

faq.question: Why is the bed temperature limited to 100°C when Prusament recommends 105-115°C?
faq.answer: The P1P hardware power supply and heated bed controller are firmware-locked to a maximum of 100°C, requiring pristine bed cleanliness, glue stick, and zero drafts to compensate.

faq.question: Does Prusament PC Blend require a hardened steel nozzle upgrade?
faq.answer: No, standard Prusament PC Blend is an unfilled polycarbonate alloy and is non-abrasive, making it completely safe for the stock stainless steel nozzle.

faq.question: Why is a glue stick strictly required when using a Textured PEI Plate?
faq.answer: Polycarbonate bonds aggressively to PEI coatings; the glue stick functions as a sacrificial release agent to prevent tearing the PEI sheet during part removal.
